title: Applied Commerce Concept Atlas
purpose: Trace the concepts underneath BIS back to Applied Commerce and make curriculum, teaching, evidence and reporting use the same semantic layer.
derivationRule: Concepts are distilled from authored Applied Commerce material and indexed to grade/lesson locations. They do not replace source prose or Lab-specific authored measures.

concepts.title: Identity and self-story
concepts.proposition: Identity is shaped by beliefs, values, experience and repeated action; it is not a fixed score.
concepts.transfer: Use evidence from another context to test whether the self-story still fits.

concepts.title: Beliefs as learned frames
concepts.proposition: Beliefs can be inherited or learned without deliberate choice and can be examined rather than simply obeyed.
concepts.transfer: Identify a belief in a second domain and trace where it came from.

concepts.title: Personal efficacy
concepts.proposition: Capability can grow through action, practice and evidence of what one can learn or do.
concepts.transfer: Use a prior success as evidence when approaching a new but related challenge.

concepts.title: Values as a decision compass
concepts.proposition: Values matter when choices create tension or cost; stated values should be compared with actual decisions.
concepts.transfer: Apply the same value to a different trade-off and explain any change.

concepts.title: Social influence
concepts.proposition: Other people, groups and social cues shape choices; influence can be noticed and evaluated.
concepts.transfer: Recognise a different influence source and choose a response deliberately.

concepts.title: Goals, intentions and direction
concepts.proposition: A meaningful goal creates direction only when translated into specific choices, actions and review.
concepts.transfer: Re-plan the same goal after a constraint changes.

concepts.title: Needs, wants and trade-offs
concepts.proposition: Scarce resources require choices; needs, wants and priorities can shift with context and consequences.
concepts.transfer: Use the distinction in a new resource-constrained decision.

concepts.title: Saving as a designed routine
concepts.proposition: Saving is more reliable when the action, timing and system are designed rather than left to intention.
concepts.transfer: Adapt the saving routine when income timing or context changes.

concepts.title: Money, exchange and value creation
concepts.proposition: Money is connected to exchange and value created; tracing value clarifies where income comes from.
concepts.transfer: Trace value and payment in a different product, service or informal activity.

concepts.title: Initiative
concepts.proposition: Agency includes noticing a solvable problem and acting without waiting for perfect permission or conditions.
concepts.transfer: Take one bounded first action in a new problem context.

concepts.title: Failure as information
concepts.proposition: A failed attempt can provide evidence about assumptions, design or conditions when the learner examines what happened.
concepts.transfer: Use evidence from a setback to revise a second attempt.

concepts.title: Accurate thinking and consequence
concepts.proposition: Choices should be distinguished from assumptions by examining evidence, alternatives and consequences.
concepts.transfer: Evaluate a new claim and state what evidence would change the conclusion.

concepts.title: Self-discipline through structure
concepts.proposition: Self-discipline is supported by routines, constraints and repeatable structures rather than treated as a personality trait.
concepts.transfer: Design a different structure for another repeated action.

concepts.title: Skills, work and assets
concepts.proposition: Skills can create value and can be developed, combined and deployed across work and enterprise contexts.
concepts.transfer: Name how one skill transfers to a different task or role.

concepts.title: Records make patterns visible
concepts.proposition: Records reduce reliance on memory and make flows, patterns, gaps and change reviewable.
concepts.transfer: Use a record in another domain and compare it with prior recall.

concepts.title: Income streams and reliability
concepts.proposition: Income sources differ in effort, reliability, dependence and scalability; a stream should be evaluated, not merely counted.
concepts.transfer: Compare a new income source on reliability, control and cost.

concepts.title: Opportunity recognition
concepts.proposition: Problems, unmet needs and changing conditions can be investigated as possible opportunities rather than assumed to be opportunities.
concepts.transfer: Test whether a different observed need represents real demand.

concepts.title: Pricing and negotiation
concepts.proposition: Price is a decision shaped by cost, value, alternatives, constraints and conversation; negotiation requires reasoned boundaries.
concepts.transfer: Negotiate or simulate a different exchange while protecting a stated boundary.

concepts.title: Spending psychology and influence
concepts.proposition: Spending is affected by emotion, social pressure, advertising and immediate reward, not only stated need.
concepts.transfer: Identify the pull behind a different purchase and design one friction point.

concepts.title: Budgeting as allocation
concepts.proposition: A budget makes priorities and trade-offs visible by allocating limited resources before or during use.
concepts.transfer: Reallocate after income, costs or priorities change.

concepts.title: Leakage and unnoticed accumulation
concepts.proposition: Small repeated uses of resources can accumulate into meaningful loss; tracking makes leakage visible.
concepts.transfer: Find and test one leakage pattern in money, time or attention.

concepts.title: Habit loop
concepts.proposition: Repeated behaviour can be examined through cues, routines and rewards rather than treated as character.
concepts.transfer: Map the same loop structure in a different habit.

concepts.title: Repetition and automaticity
concepts.proposition: Repeated responses can become easier or more automatic; the conditions around repetition matter.
concepts.transfer: Repeat a small response in a new suitable context and compare friction.

concepts.title: Accountability and social support
concepts.proposition: Support structures and shared expectations can make follow-through easier without replacing personal responsibility.
concepts.transfer: Test a different accountability arrangement and compare what changes.

concepts.title: Small steps and compounding
concepts.proposition: Small repeated actions can create larger cumulative effects over time; compounding also amplifies poor patterns.
concepts.transfer: Project and then observe a small repeated action across a longer window.

concepts.title: Consistency, setbacks and recovery
concepts.proposition: Progress does not require perfection; recovery after disruption is part of a sustainable behaviour system.
concepts.transfer: Use a restart plan after a different interruption.

concepts.title: Identity through evidence
concepts.proposition: Repeated actions create evidence about who a learner is becoming, but evidence should remain open to revision.
concepts.transfer: Compare identity claims with a second body of behavioural evidence.

concepts.title: Planning and prioritisation
concepts.proposition: Planning converts priorities into ordered actions and protects what matters from lower-value demands.
concepts.transfer: Reprioritise under a new deadline or constraint.

concepts.title: Time audit and attention allocation
concepts.proposition: Time use becomes investigable when activity is recorded; attention allocation, not memory alone, reveals where time went.
concepts.transfer: Run a second audit in another context and compare memory with record.

concepts.title: Start friction and procrastination
concepts.proposition: Delay can arise from fear, overwhelm, perfectionism, immediate reward or genuine lack of capacity; the intervention must match the cause.
concepts.transfer: Test a smaller first step or a condition change and compare what happened.

concepts.title: Decision process
concepts.proposition: A strong decision makes criteria, alternatives, trade-offs, evidence and consequences explicit.
concepts.transfer: Use the same decision structure for a different choice.

concepts.title: Resilience as internal and external resources
concepts.proposition: Recovery depends on both internal capacities and external resources; barriers are not automatically evidence of weak character.
concepts.transfer: Audit resources for a different disruption and identify one support need.

concepts.title: Growth mindset and revisable ability
concepts.proposition: Learning can change capability, but growth claims should be tied to practice, feedback and evidence rather than slogans.
concepts.transfer: Use feedback to revise performance in another task.

concepts.title: Enterprise as value exchange
concepts.proposition: Enterprise connects a real need, a customer, a useful offer, resources, costs and a way to learn from response.
concepts.transfer: Test the value proposition with a different customer or assumption.

concepts.title: Value chains and community systems
concepts.proposition: Products, services and money move through connected actors; benefits, dependencies and leakage can be traced.
concepts.transfer: Map another chain and identify who depends on whom.

concepts.title: Systems thinking
concepts.proposition: Outcomes emerge from connected parts, relationships and feedback; changing one part can create wider effects.
concepts.transfer: Map a different system and predict at least one ripple effect.

concepts.title: Automation, defaults and friction
concepts.proposition: A system can make desired actions easier and repeated decisions less dependent on willpower by changing defaults or friction.
concepts.transfer: Create or simulate a default in a second repeated process.

concepts.title: Leverage points
concepts.proposition: Some points in a system produce disproportionate effects; leverage should be identified, tested and monitored for unintended consequences.
concepts.transfer: Test a different leverage point and compare ripple effects.

concepts.title: Risk and return
concepts.proposition: Potential gain and potential loss should be considered together; risk is not removed by optimism.
concepts.transfer: Compare a second option on downside, uncertainty and response.

concepts.title: Assets and liabilities
concepts.proposition: Resources and commitments differ in whether they support or drain future capacity; classification depends on context and use.
concepts.transfer: Classify a new item and explain the conditions under which the classification could change.

concepts.title: Debt and credit
concepts.proposition: Debt can be a tool or a trap depending on purpose, terms, affordability, risk and repayment capacity.
concepts.transfer: Evaluate a different credit scenario and name the missing information.

concepts.title: Investing and long horizons
concepts.proposition: Investment decisions require purpose, risk, time horizon, assumptions, diversification and review rather than return chasing.
concepts.transfer: Compare another investment scenario with a different horizon or risk tolerance.

concepts.title: Self-leadership and leadership
concepts.proposition: Leadership begins with self-management and extends to decisions that affect other people.
concepts.transfer: Lead or simulate a different team situation and review the effect on others.

concepts.title: Communication and difficult conversations
concepts.proposition: Useful communication combines clarity, listening, questions, boundaries and responsible handling of disagreement.
concepts.transfer: Adapt the message and listening approach to a different audience or tension.

concepts.title: Influence and pressure
concepts.proposition: Influence can change choices through social proof, authority, belonging, emotion or urgency; deliberate decisions require noticing the pressure.
concepts.transfer: Identify a different influence mechanism and choose a deliberate response.

concepts.title: Ethics, trust and responsibility
concepts.proposition: Trust is built or damaged through repeated choices, transparency, fairness and responsibility for consequences.
concepts.transfer: Reason through a new ethical tension and state who bears the consequences.

concepts.title: Time leverage
concepts.proposition: Time can be multiplied through prioritisation, batching, systematisation, automation, delegation and elimination, while accountability remains.
concepts.transfer: Apply one leverage method in a second context and review the cost or responsibility it creates.

concepts.title: Delegation, teams and accountability
concepts.proposition: Delegating a task changes who performs it but does not automatically remove responsibility for the system or outcome.
concepts.transfer: Delegate or simulate delegation of a different task and review quality, trust and accountability.

concepts.title: Long-term thinking and legacy
concepts.proposition: Present choices compound into future options and impact; longer horizons require explicit trade-offs and responsibility.
concepts.transfer: Trace second-order consequences of a different present choice.

concepts.title: Career navigation and opportunity pathways
concepts.proposition: Career movement involves skills, evidence, relationships, communication, persistence and more than one possible pathway.
concepts.transfer: Build and test a next-step pathway in another role or learning route.

concepts.title: Transition and launch
concepts.proposition: A transition plan connects intention to logistics, resources, timing, risk, support and next actions in a real context.
concepts.transfer: Revise the plan after a changed assumption or new constraint.

concepts.title: Protection, failure signals and recovery
concepts.proposition: A robust plan states what could fail, what observable signal would reveal failure, and what response or support follows.
concepts.transfer: Stress-test a second scenario and revise one assumption.

concepts.title: Reflection, revision and transfer
concepts.proposition: Learning becomes more useful when evidence is reviewed, an explanation is revised and the method is carried into another context.
concepts.transfer: Demonstrate the method in a meaningfully different context and explain limits.

concepts.title: Evidence types and uncertainty
concepts.proposition: Predictions, plans, explanations, simulations, observations and outcomes answer different questions and must not be collapsed into one proof claim.
concepts.transfer: Reclassify evidence from another task and state what each item can and cannot support.

concepts.title: Iteration and innovation
concepts.proposition: Improvement comes from identifying a gap, testing a response, learning from feedback and iterating rather than waiting for a perfect first solution.
concepts.transfer: Run another small iteration and explain why the revision is justified.

concepts.title: Customer thinking
concepts.proposition: Value is judged in relation to a customer's need, context and alternatives; creator assumptions require testing.
concepts.transfer: Interview, observe or simulate a different customer context and revise the offer.

concepts.title: Professional communication and personal brand
concepts.proposition: How work and capability are communicated affects access to opportunities; evidence should support the story being told.
concepts.transfer: Adapt the same evidence for a different professional audience.

concepts.title: Economics, incentives and human behaviour
concepts.proposition: Economic patterns reflect flows, constraints, incentives and human behaviour inside systems rather than isolated numbers.
concepts.transfer: Explain a different local economic pattern using incentives and relationships.

concepts.title: Transferable skills and adaptability
concepts.proposition: A skill can create value across different roles when the learner can identify the underlying capability and adapt its use.
concepts.transfer: Demonstrate the same underlying skill in a different task.

concepts.title: Meta-learning
concepts.proposition: Learners improve learning by examining how they learn, using feedback, selecting strategies and reviewing what evidence shows.
concepts.transfer: Choose a different learning strategy for a new task and compare results.
